{"milestones":[{"id":"cb9c8236-7ea7-404c-b9b6-641d87b398d3","name":"Extraction v2","description":"Extraction that can be trusted and extended per site. A generic base extraction plus declarative per-domain recipes (substack, medium and similar behave the same once described), an agent loop that writes a recipe for an unknown site, auto-validation gates that fail an item whose extraction is not the article before anyone has to report it, and a per-recipe fetch strategy (direct fetch with a browser user agent, firecrawl, or a real browser) with firecrawl kept as a pluggable backend.

Build order: validation gates, then recipe schema and resolver, then the agent recipe loop, then fetch pluggability, then a reporting UI only if still needed. Paywalled credentials are deferred, possibly forever.

This replaces an earlier plan that put an LLM in the extraction hot path (firecrawl always, HTML always, an LLM instead of trafilatura, with a prompt eval system). The recipes approach keeps per-request extraction deterministic and moves the intelligence to authoring time.","progress":50,"sortOrder":53},{"id":"dec22a7f-5f2d-4690-bc1c-60c6c84a1156","name":"Validate demand","description":"Find out whether anyone besides the owner wants a private audio read-later queue. The milestone is complete when a stranger has come to nagara, queued a real item, and come back.

Everything else in the repository exists to make this answerable. The backend spine (enqueue, extraction, TTS, markdown-formatted paragraphs) is built and proven, and the compute cost is settled at roughly $0.008 per article (`docs/technical-design/tts-service.md`). What is unproven is the product shape and whether there is an audience.

The surface in question is what a stranger meets: the funnel (landing page, login, article creation), the queue, and the player. Extraction internals and TTS cost are settled and not part of this. Read `docs/product-design/what-nagara-is.md` for what is deliberately out of MVP scope and `docs/product-design/queue.md` ("what is not built yet") for the build order agreed on 2026-07-17.

Decisions already settled:

* The public-funnel work (real auth, onboarding, a landing page) exists in service of this question and nothing else.
* Pricing waits until there is an audience to price for; the pricing model is a separate open item that depends on this one.
* A builder-driven loop validates shape, never demand, and must not be presented as validated demand. This was learned during the read-along player shape spike.

Candidate experiments once strangers can reach nagara, not yet phrased as single tasks:

* Whether a paste-a-URL public hook converts a stranger into a first queued item.
* Whether a bundle-of-items or a metered-audio-minutes framing reads better.
* What a stranger does on their second visit.
* Whether an acquisition surface such as a save-to-nagara bookmarklet changes any of that.

Out of scope: multi-user scaling before validation (quota, key management, and multi-user behaviour are worth building only if the answer is yes), and pricing before an audience.","progress":0,"sortOrder":976},{"id":"fc4a00b7-fc99-49df-962f-09966bfa3636","name":"Formulas read aloud","description":"Every formula an article carries reaches a listener as speech and a client as raw LaTeX. No formula is silent and none is read aloud as syntax. Done means the five measured families pass through end to end, each with a fixture and each played once: MathML inline (arXiv/LaTeXML), MathML display (Wikipedia), `$$…$$` inside a bare `<div>` (lilianweng), the raw `$…$` leak (lilianweng) and the raw `\(…\)` leak (colah).

Decisions already settled by the design work, with the measurements behind them:

* Recovery happens once, at the single `trafilatura.extract` seam inside `_extract_units_from_html` in `api/app/service/extract.py`, via a text carrier, so the plain fetch and the firecrawl fallback both get it. Recovery rewrites the HTML handed to trafilatura; it never re-extracts. `extract_article` keeps returning the original `page.html`, because `images.py` probes that tree and `extract_metadata` reads it for the title.
* The outermost math wrapper is replaced, never the `<math>` node: replacing the node recovers 0 of 99 formulas on Wikipedia, because MediaWiki hides the MathML in an a11y wrapper trafilatura discards.
* A fourth typed unit, `FormulaUnit`, carries raw LaTeX in `display` and the bare TeX in `latex`.
* Inline math is verbalized in place by a hand-rolled rules table. Display math is described on the existing describe budget with the verbalized LaTeX as its floor. A formula never fails the item and is never dropped.
* No LaTeX-to-speech library: `latex2speech`, `mathspeak`, `speech-rule-engine` and `mathml2speech` are absent from PyPI, and `pylatexenc` produces unicode Kokoro cannot read.
* No formula equivalent of the code path's "every one failed" raise.

Code involved: a new `api/app/service/formulas.py`, plus `extract.py`, `describe.py`, the anchor probe in `images.py`, and `api/app/schemas/items.py`. `tts/` is untouched: it receives a list of spoken strings and that contract does not change. `web/` is not built here.

The notes `docs/technical-design/article-extraction.md`, `docs/technical-design/item-contract.md`, `docs/technical-design/the-describer.md` and `docs/product-design/what-gets-read-aloud.md` are written once, at the end, out of all the finished work rather than per task.

Out of scope:

* Formulas rendered to images with no MathML twin and no usable alt (some Substack and Medium posts). No LaTeX exists to recover; the image path already gives them a described `ImageUnit`.
* A page rendering bare `$…$` while declaring no math renderer. Nothing distinguishes it from "between $5 and $10 million"; the residual is accepted.
* The KaTeX renderer in `web/`. Raw LaTeX in `display` is a commitment made on behalf of a client nobody has written; honouring it belongs to whoever builds `web/`.
* Replacing the verbalizer with a library. None exists; one appearing later is one of the things that would make this shape stop being true.","progress":25,"sortOrder":1948},{"id":"4232272a-96de-4304-8664-688c8187dafd","name":"Read-along player","description":"A web surface at `web/` where an item's audio and its text are read together, the text following the audio closely enough that listening while reading is one activity rather than two. One player with two reading modes: a calm scroll-normal reader by default, and an opt-in focus mode that centres and enlarges the active paragraph. It consumes the existing item contract unchanged: no per-unit `type` field, no word-level timing, nothing in `api/` or `tts/`. Done means the surface is built, deployed and dogfooded on real generated items, with its mechanism recorded as a note in `docs/technical-design/`.

Decisions settled by the spike, which is preserved on the unmerged `idea/read-along-player` branch with its tree relocated to `web/`:

* The stack is TanStack Start with Panda-CSS. The build is a rewrite of the spike, not a merge.
* A dark immersive shell with a heading-derived floating table of contents, a floating transport and a progress bar.
* Scroll-decoupled navigation: a seek-to-here follow pill, ±10 s skip, and resume. No click-to-seek.
* Highlight sync runs off `requestAnimationFrame` polling `currentTime`, never `timeupdate`. Measured lag was 19 to 26 ms against a 200 ms budget, re-locking immediately after a seek.
* Two things from the spike must not be copied: its global `ka-*` CSS class names, which leaked between components once, and its localStorage resume, which is a stand-in rather than a decision.

Read first: `docs/product-design/listening-experience.md`, `docs/technical-design/read-along-timing.md` (timing mechanism and the seek nudge), `docs/technical-design/item-contract.md`, and `docs/technical-design/invariants.md` for the sync budget.

Open questions, each blocking a slice rather than the whole build: how lists, code and tables behave in focus mode, since centring and enlarging breaks their left-aligned structure; whether blockquote and table render and highlight correctly, since the spike's probe for them was never built; whether the mobile breakpoint holds on a real device; whether resume needs a server-side position to follow a listener across devices; how an image unit renders without being treated as prose.

The shape evidence is builder-confounded: the same person built and judged the spike on two real articles. It validates shape, UX and the functional contract, not demand or a fresh user's experience; those belong to the demand-validation work.

Out of scope: visual design (typography, colour, motion and brand feel are a separate milestone that treats this layout as fixed; the spike's placeholder aesthetic carries no verdict weight); click-to-seek (whether its absence is felt as friction by anyone other than the builder is a demand question); word-level highlighting (the contract is paragraph-level and nothing needed finer); caption export, which maps the same timing windows onto cue timings and is its own issue.","progress":25,"sortOrder":2885},{"id":"5d1d2f53-65e7-4600-bb34-bcd3bbd183b7","name":"Read-along visual design","description":"A proper visual design for the read-along player and, by extension, the web surface: a design language, typography, colour, motion, and light and dark modes, coherent enough that a stranger reads it as a finished product. Judged on aesthetic coherence and quality against real long-form articles rather than sample text, because sustained prose is where typography either works or does not.

Already settled and not up for redesign: the player's layout, navigation and structure. The shape work fixed one player with a calm scroll-normal default and an opt-in focus mode, inside a dark immersive shell with a heading-derived floating table of contents, a floating transport, a progress bar and a scroll-decoupled follow pill, with no click-to-seek. That shape is the fixed substrate this effort must not disturb. If a visual direction seems to require changing it, record the finding; it is not a licence to change the shape.

The placeholder aesthetic the shape was validated against carried no verdict weight and is not a starting point. Treat it as absent rather than as a first draft.

Read first: the spike on the unmerged `idea/read-along-player` branch (tree at `web/`) for what is settled, the read-along player milestone for the surface itself, and `docs/product-design/listening-experience.md` for what the product is meant to feel like.","progress":0,"sortOrder":3899},{"id":"d33627be-4943-48ff-90f7-a22b2f1fc420","name":"ORM relationships","description":"Declare the mapped relationships across the models instead of the flat FK-only pattern: items to recipe_versions, items to cost_entries, and whatever else the schema joins. Writes assign through the relationship attributes so SQLAlchemy's unit of work orders inserts and updates by dependency rather than by table order, the manual flush in insert_recipe_version retires, and the queued phase's guarded writes get a second look under autoflush with related objects in play. Born from the production foreign-key incident (commit f02f5b0); to be explored and shaped before building.","progress":0,"sortOrder":4810},{"id":"8f6c74e7-9314-4d0e-b5c8-fd144f08a8b0","name":"Markdown and lists","description":"Improve what the extraction and TTS pipeline outputs, from both ends: the markdown a recipe extracts, and how that markdown is read aloud.

* Markdown fidelity: recipes extract real structure (blockquotes when the text is a quote, headings, lists) instead of flattening everything to plain paragraphs. Verified with a synthetic article that exercises every markdown element, run through each recipe; the structure must come out intact.
* Lists in audio: a list is currently read as one paragraph with no breaks. Each item becomes its own unit or chunk, so the TTS delivers it as a list rather than a run-on paragraph.

To be shaped and designed before tasks are written.","progress":91.67,"sortOrder":5788},{"id":"1f715c70-f21d-466d-92a3-ef263db6955e","name":"Cloudflare migration","description":"Move the rest of nagara onto Cloudflare, so the recipe logic and the articles extracted with older recipes live in one place. The extraction pipeline already runs on Cloudflare (`pipeline/`); what else moves is not settled yet.

Recipe reconciliation depends on this milestone.

To be shaped and designed before tasks are written.","progress":0,"sortOrder":6718},{"id":"a8dac438-de5f-47de-bd28-842f492249b9","name":"Recipe reconciliation","description":"Stop recipes for one domain from replacing each other. A domain that publishes more than one article format can end up with two recipes bouncing back and forth, because each one matches only one format.

When a domain's recipe is tested, its previous recipes are tested too. If an older recipe still matches, a reconciliation prompt merges the variants into one recipe that covers both.

Depends on the Cloudflare migration: building a recipe that matches both variants needs the recipe logic and the articles extracted with older recipes in one place.

To be shaped and designed before tasks are written.","progress":0,"sortOrder":7684}]}

The current milestone isn't finished yet. **Markdown and lists** is at 92%, and ASE-70 (hand-edit the four stored recipes that break the markdown rules) is still In Progress. I'd close that first.

After that, I'd take **Formulas read aloud** (25%). Its design task (ASE-36) is done and it has three implementation tasks waiting:
- ASE-37: MathML recovered into a `FormulaUnit` and spoken by the verbalizer (High)
- ASE-39: Raw math delimiters and math/tex scripts recovered (High)
- ASE-38: Display formulas described on the shared describe budget (Medium)

**Its design is out of date, though.** The milestone puts formula recovery at "the single `trafilatura.extract` seam inside `_extract_units_from_html` in `api/app/service/extract.py`". Neither of those exists in `api/app` anymore, because Extraction v2 moved extraction into recipes running in `pipeline/` on Cloudflare. Recovery now probably belongs in the pipeline's runtime or in the authoring prompts. So the formula design needs another pass, probably a short `mahou:design` session, before ASE-37/38/39 can be built as written.

The other milestones:
- **Extraction v2** (50%): ASE-10, X-post extraction losing images, code blocks and structure, is marked Todo at High priority. This is the one to pick if you'd rather do a self-contained fix than redo the formula design.
- **Read-along player** (25%): the shape spike is done, and ASE-41 (the surface itself) is ready to build.
- **Read-along visual design**: waits on the player.
- **Recipe reconciliation**: depends on **Cloudflare migration**, which hasn't been shaped yet.
- **ORM relationships**: hasn't been shaped yet.
- **Validate demand**: needs the web surfaces first.

entries.name: mcp__linear-server__get_issue
entries.description: Retrieve detailed information about an issue by ID, including attachments, git branch name, and active Triage Intelligence suggestions when the issue is in triage

id.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues

entries.name: mcp__linear-server__list_comments
entries.description: List comments on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. Provide exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId`. For issues, projects, and initiatives this returns both top-level discussion threads and inline description comments. Inline (anchored) comments carry a non-null `quotedText` set to the snippet of description text they reference. Returned comments include `author` and nullable `onBehalfOf`; when set, `onBehalfOf` identifies the user the agent author acted for. Files uploaded in comment bodies are returned in `attachments` with titles and download URLs, not issue attachment IDs. Signed upload URLs expire after five minutes; call list_comments again to refresh them. Download documents using these URLs and process them with your own file tools.

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Only valid together with `statusUpdateId`; omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

entries.name: mcp__linear-server__save_issue
entries.description: Create or update a Linear issue. If `id` is provided, updates the existing issue; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `team` is required, and `title` is required unless `template` is set. Note: use `assignee` (not `assigneeId`) to set the assignee — it accepts a user ID, name, email, or "me".

id.description: Only for updating an existing issue. Pass the issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Do NOT pass this parameter when creating a new issue.

title.description: Issue title (required when creating, unless template is set)

description.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe)

patch.description: Partial edits applied to the current content, in order and atomically (one failing operation aborts the whole save). Every anchor string must match the current content exactly once. Only valid on update, in place of the full content/description field

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Must match the current content exactly once

new_string.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the match

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match

anchor.description: Exact text to insert before. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly before the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")

anchor.description: Exact text to insert after. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly after the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")
Text to insert at the very start of the content
Text to insert at the very end of the content

from.description: Exact text where the range starts (inclusive). Must match exactly once

to.description: Exact text where the range ends (exclusive, stays in place). Must match exactly once after `from`

new_string.description: Text replacing the range. Empty string deletes it

team.description: Team name or ID (required when creating)

template.description: Template name or ID. Applied on create only. The template fills in the content, fields, and sub-issues server-side. A `description` replaces the template body rather than merging with it, but an empty `description` keeps the template body. Labels merge with the template's own

cycle.description: Cycle name, number, or ID. Null to remove

project.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug. Null to remove

assignee.description: User ID, name, email, or "me". Null to remove

delegate.description: Agent name or ID. When the user asks to delegate to "Linear" or "the Linear agent", this refers to the "Linear" app user specifically. Null to remove

labels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]). Replaces the full label set; existing labels not included are removed. Omit to leave labels unchanged. Cannot be combined with addLabels/removeLabels; prefer those for incremental changes

addLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to add. Append-only; existing labels are never removed. Cannot be combined with a team change

removeLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue. Cannot be combined with a team change

dueDate.description: Due date (ISO format). On update, pass null to remove the due date

slaBreachesAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the SLA will breach. On update, pass null to remove the SLA

slaType.description: SLA day counting type: "all" or "onlyBusinessDays". Only use with slaBreachesAt; null means unset

parentId.description: Parent issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Null to remove

estimate.description: Issue estimate value. On create, pass null or omit for no estimate. On update, pass null to clear the estimate; omitting leaves it unchanged. 0 is a real estimate only on teams that allow zero estimates.

links.description: Link attachments to add [{url, title}]. Append-only; existing links are never removed

setReleases.description: Replace all releases on the issue with these. Cannot be combined with addReleases/removeReleases

addReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to add. Append-only; existing releases are never removed

removeReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue

blocks.description: Issue IDs/identifiers this blocks. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

blockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers blocking this. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

relatedTo.description: Related issue IDs/identifiers. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

duplicateOf.description: Duplicate of issue ID/identifier. Null to remove

removeBlockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers to remove as blockers of this issue

I haven't changed anything in Linear yet, because I couldn't confirm the recipe edits.

**Why it's unconfirmed:** ASE-70 says to overwrite the stored recipe rows in the production database. Those rows aren't in git, and the issue has no comments recording the work. I tried a read-only query of `recipe_versions` through `railway run`, but the permission classifier blocked reads against production.

**What to look for:** the latest version of each domain's recipe should have a `created_at` after 2026-09-28 (the day ASE-70 was created) and fix what the issue lists:
- **blog.dyanacek.com**: no longer declares one `<li>` per unit.
- **newsletter.pragmaticengineer.com**: no longer declares one `<li>` per unit, and hands the whole blockquote as one unit instead of walking its children.
- **harper.blog**: leaves `h1` out of the body headings and drops the catch-all fallback.
- **ngrislain.github.io**: keeps `<ul>` whole instead of letting the recursive fallback split it by its descendants.

You can run this yourself so the output lands in the conversation:

```
! cd api && railway run -- uv run python -c "import asyncio; from sqlalchemy import text; from app.models import engine
async def m():
    async with engine.connect() as c:
        for d in ['blog.dyanacek.com','newsletter.pragmaticengineer.com','harper.blog','ngrislain.github.io']:
            r = (await c.execute(text('select version, created_at, script from recipe_versions where domain=:d order by version desc limit 1'), {'d': d})).one_or_none()
            print('=====', d, r and (r.version, r.created_at)); print(r and r.script)
asyncio.run(m())"
```

Or you can add a permission rule that allows production reads. Once I can see the scripts, I'll check them against the list above and close ASE-70.

Linear has no "done" state for a milestone. A milestone counts as complete when all its issues are done, and ASE-70 is the only open one in Markdown and lists. Closing ASE-70 therefore completes the milestone.

ASE-70 also asks for B19: one real pragmaticengineer article run through production and listened to. Only you can confirm that one. Have you done it?

{"milestones":[{"id":"cb9c8236-7ea7-404c-b9b6-641d87b398d3","name":"Extraction v2","description":"Extraction that can be trusted and extended per site. A generic base extraction plus declarative per-domain recipes (substack, medium and similar behave the same once described), an agent loop that writes a recipe for an unknown site, auto-validation gates that fail an item whose extraction is not the article before anyone has to report it, and a per-recipe fetch strategy (direct fetch with a browser user agent, firecrawl, or a real browser) with firecrawl kept as a pluggable backend.

Build order: validation gates, then recipe schema and resolver, then the agent recipe loop, then fetch pluggability, then a reporting UI only if still needed. Paywalled credentials are deferred, possibly forever.

This replaces an earlier plan that put an LLM in the extraction hot path (firecrawl always, HTML always, an LLM instead of trafilatura, with a prompt eval system). The recipes approach keeps per-request extraction deterministic and moves the intelligence to authoring time.","progress":50,"sortOrder":53},{"id":"dec22a7f-5f2d-4690-bc1c-60c6c84a1156","name":"Validate demand","description":"Find out whether anyone besides the owner wants a private audio read-later queue. The milestone is complete when a stranger has come to nagara, queued a real item, and come back.

Everything else in the repository exists to make this answerable. The backend spine (enqueue, extraction, TTS, markdown-formatted paragraphs) is built and proven, and the compute cost is settled at roughly $0.008 per article (`docs/technical-design/tts-service.md`). What is unproven is the product shape and whether there is an audience.

The surface in question is what a stranger meets: the funnel (landing page, login, article creation), the queue, and the player. Extraction internals and TTS cost are settled and not part of this. Read `docs/product-design/what-nagara-is.md` for what is deliberately out of MVP scope and `docs/product-design/queue.md` ("what is not built yet") for the build order agreed on 2026-07-17.

Decisions already settled:

* The public-funnel work (real auth, onboarding, a landing page) exists in service of this question and nothing else.
* Pricing waits until there is an audience to price for; the pricing model is a separate open item that depends on this one.
* A builder-driven loop validates shape, never demand, and must not be presented as validated demand. This was learned during the read-along player shape spike.

Candidate experiments once strangers can reach nagara, not yet phrased as single tasks:

* Whether a paste-a-URL public hook converts a stranger into a first queued item.
* Whether a bundle-of-items or a metered-audio-minutes framing reads better.
* What a stranger does on their second visit.
* Whether an acquisition surface such as a save-to-nagara bookmarklet changes any of that.

Out of scope: multi-user scaling before validation (quota, key management, and multi-user behaviour are worth building only if the answer is yes), and pricing before an audience.","progress":0,"sortOrder":976},{"id":"fc4a00b7-fc99-49df-962f-09966bfa3636","name":"Formulas read aloud","description":"Every formula an article carries reaches a listener as speech and a client as raw LaTeX. No formula is silent and none is read aloud as syntax. Done means the five measured families pass through end to end, each with a fixture and each played once: MathML inline (arXiv/LaTeXML), MathML display (Wikipedia), `$$…$$` inside a bare `<div>` (lilianweng), the raw `$…$` leak (lilianweng) and the raw `\(…\)` leak (colah).

Decisions already settled by the design work, with the measurements behind them:

* Recovery happens once, at the single `trafilatura.extract` seam inside `_extract_units_from_html` in `api/app/service/extract.py`, via a text carrier, so the plain fetch and the firecrawl fallback both get it. Recovery rewrites the HTML handed to trafilatura; it never re-extracts. `extract_article` keeps returning the original `page.html`, because `images.py` probes that tree and `extract_metadata` reads it for the title.
* The outermost math wrapper is replaced, never the `<math>` node: replacing the node recovers 0 of 99 formulas on Wikipedia, because MediaWiki hides the MathML in an a11y wrapper trafilatura discards.
* A fourth typed unit, `FormulaUnit`, carries raw LaTeX in `display` and the bare TeX in `latex`.
* Inline math is verbalized in place by a hand-rolled rules table. Display math is described on the existing describe budget with the verbalized LaTeX as its floor. A formula never fails the item and is never dropped.
* No LaTeX-to-speech library: `latex2speech`, `mathspeak`, `speech-rule-engine` and `mathml2speech` are absent from PyPI, and `pylatexenc` produces unicode Kokoro cannot read.
* No formula equivalent of the code path's "every one failed" raise.

Code involved: a new `api/app/service/formulas.py`, plus `extract.py`, `describe.py`, the anchor probe in `images.py`, and `api/app/schemas/items.py`. `tts/` is untouched: it receives a list of spoken strings and that contract does not change. `web/` is not built here.

The notes `docs/technical-design/article-extraction.md`, `docs/technical-design/item-contract.md`, `docs/technical-design/the-describer.md` and `docs/product-design/what-gets-read-aloud.md` are written once, at the end, out of all the finished work rather than per task.

Out of scope:

* Formulas rendered to images with no MathML twin and no usable alt (some Substack and Medium posts). No LaTeX exists to recover; the image path already gives them a described `ImageUnit`.
* A page rendering bare `$…$` while declaring no math renderer. Nothing distinguishes it from "between $5 and $10 million"; the residual is accepted.
* The KaTeX renderer in `web/`. Raw LaTeX in `display` is a commitment made on behalf of a client nobody has written; honouring it belongs to whoever builds `web/`.
* Replacing the verbalizer with a library. None exists; one appearing later is one of the things that would make this shape stop being true.","progress":25,"sortOrder":1948},{"id":"4232272a-96de-4304-8664-688c8187dafd","name":"Read-along player","description":"A web surface at `web/` where an item's audio and its text are read together, the text following the audio closely enough that listening while reading is one activity rather than two. One player with two reading modes: a calm scroll-normal reader by default, and an opt-in focus mode that centres and enlarges the active paragraph. It consumes the existing item contract unchanged: no per-unit `type` field, no word-level timing, nothing in `api/` or `tts/`. Done means the surface is built, deployed and dogfooded on real generated items, with its mechanism recorded as a note in `docs/technical-design/`.

Decisions settled by the spike, which is preserved on the unmerged `idea/read-along-player` branch with its tree relocated to `web/`:

* The stack is TanStack Start with Panda-CSS. The build is a rewrite of the spike, not a merge.
* A dark immersive shell with a heading-derived floating table of contents, a floating transport and a progress bar.
* Scroll-decoupled navigation: a seek-to-here follow pill, ±10 s skip, and resume. No click-to-seek.
* Highlight sync runs off `requestAnimationFrame` polling `currentTime`, never `timeupdate`. Measured lag was 19 to 26 ms against a 200 ms budget, re-locking immediately after a seek.
* Two things from the spike must not be copied: its global `ka-*` CSS class names, which leaked between components once, and its localStorage resume, which is a stand-in rather than a decision.

Read first: `docs/product-design/listening-experience.md`, `docs/technical-design/read-along-timing.md` (timing mechanism and the seek nudge), `docs/technical-design/item-contract.md`, and `docs/technical-design/invariants.md` for the sync budget.

Open questions, each blocking a slice rather than the whole build: how lists, code and tables behave in focus mode, since centring and enlarging breaks their left-aligned structure; whether blockquote and table render and highlight correctly, since the spike's probe for them was never built; whether the mobile breakpoint holds on a real device; whether resume needs a server-side position to follow a listener across devices; how an image unit renders without being treated as prose.

The shape evidence is builder-confounded: the same person built and judged the spike on two real articles. It validates shape, UX and the functional contract, not demand or a fresh user's experience; those belong to the demand-validation work.

Out of scope: visual design (typography, colour, motion and brand feel are a separate milestone that treats this layout as fixed; the spike's placeholder aesthetic carries no verdict weight); click-to-seek (whether its absence is felt as friction by anyone other than the builder is a demand question); word-level highlighting (the contract is paragraph-level and nothing needed finer); caption export, which maps the same timing windows onto cue timings and is its own issue.","progress":25,"sortOrder":2885},{"id":"5d1d2f53-65e7-4600-bb34-bcd3bbd183b7","name":"Read-along visual design","description":"A proper visual design for the read-along player and, by extension, the web surface: a design language, typography, colour, motion, and light and dark modes, coherent enough that a stranger reads it as a finished product. Judged on aesthetic coherence and quality against real long-form articles rather than sample text, because sustained prose is where typography either works or does not.

Already settled and not up for redesign: the player's layout, navigation and structure. The shape work fixed one player with a calm scroll-normal default and an opt-in focus mode, inside a dark immersive shell with a heading-derived floating table of contents, a floating transport, a progress bar and a scroll-decoupled follow pill, with no click-to-seek. That shape is the fixed substrate this effort must not disturb. If a visual direction seems to require changing it, record the finding; it is not a licence to change the shape.

The placeholder aesthetic the shape was validated against carried no verdict weight and is not a starting point. Treat it as absent rather than as a first draft.

Read first: the spike on the unmerged `idea/read-along-player` branch (tree at `web/`) for what is settled, the read-along player milestone for the surface itself, and `docs/product-design/listening-experience.md` for what the product is meant to feel like.","progress":0,"sortOrder":3899},{"id":"d33627be-4943-48ff-90f7-a22b2f1fc420","name":"ORM relationships","description":"Declare the mapped relationships across the models instead of the flat FK-only pattern: items to recipe_versions, items to cost_entries, and whatever else the schema joins. Writes assign through the relationship attributes so SQLAlchemy's unit of work orders inserts and updates by dependency rather than by table order, the manual flush in insert_recipe_version retires, and the queued phase's guarded writes get a second look under autoflush with related objects in play. Born from the production foreign-key incident (commit f02f5b0); to be explored and shaped before building.","progress":0,"sortOrder":4810},{"id":"8f6c74e7-9314-4d0e-b5c8-fd144f08a8b0","name":"Markdown and lists","description":"Improve what the extraction and TTS pipeline outputs, from both ends: the markdown a recipe extracts, and how that markdown is read aloud.

* Markdown fidelity: recipes extract real structure (blockquotes when the text is a quote, headings, lists) instead of flattening everything to plain paragraphs. Verified with a synthetic article that exercises every markdown element, run through each recipe; the structure must come out intact.
* Lists in audio: a list is currently read as one paragraph with no breaks. Each item becomes its own unit or chunk, so the TTS delivers it as a list rather than a run-on paragraph.

To be shaped and designed before tasks are written.","progress":100,"sortOrder":5788},{"id":"1f715c70-f21d-466d-92a3-ef263db6955e","name":"Cloudflare migration","description":"Move the rest of nagara onto Cloudflare, so the recipe logic and the articles extracted with older recipes live in one place. The extraction pipeline already runs on Cloudflare (`pipeline/`); what else moves is not settled yet.

Recipe reconciliation depends on this milestone.

To be shaped and designed before tasks are written.","progress":0,"sortOrder":6718},{"id":"a8dac438-de5f-47de-bd28-842f492249b9","name":"Recipe reconciliation","description":"Stop recipes for one domain from replacing each other. A domain that publishes more than one article format can end up with two recipes bouncing back and forth, because each one matches only one format.

When a domain's recipe is tested, its previous recipes are tested too. If an older recipe still matches, a reconciliation prompt merges the variants into one recipe that covers both.

Depends on the Cloudflare migration: building a recipe that matches both variants needs the recipe logic and the articles extracted with older recipes in one place.

To be shaped and designed before tasks are written.","progress":0,"sortOrder":7684}]}

Yes, it's the **Cloudflare migration** milestone, and nothing has been done on it yet: 0% progress, no issues, and the docs don't mention it. Its description:

> Move the rest of nagara onto Cloudflare, so the recipe logic and the articles extracted with older recipes live in one place. The extraction pipeline already runs on Cloudflare (`pipeline/`); what else moves is not settled yet.
>
> Recipe reconciliation depends on this milestone.
>
> To be shaped and designed before tasks are written.

It was created to unblock **Recipe reconciliation**. Merging two variants of one domain's recipe requires the recipe logic in `pipeline/` (Cloudflare) and the stored recipes and items (Postgres on Railway) to be in one place. That split is also why checking ASE-70 took a production database read from Railway while the recipes run on Cloudflare.

Nothing has been decided about what moves. That includes the API on Railway, Postgres (to D1 or Hyperdrive), audio storage (S3 to R2), and whether TTS stays on Modal, which is likely since it needs a GPU. Per the work-tracking rules, the next step is a `mahou:shape` session to settle the scope, then `mahou:design`, before any tasks get written.

{"id":"ASE-27","uuid":"21e4b4fc-5c22-47f2-a0fb-790d8a561939","title":"Footnote markers written as plain text are read aloud","description":"A footnote marker written as plain text carries no markup to prune, survives to synthesis, and is read aloud.

Footnote reference markers are stripped structurally today, by pruning the identifying markup out of the HTML before extraction. A marker with no markup around it is outside that reach: a `[1]` typed into the prose as ordinary text, or a bare digit left behind by a shape the xpath list does not enumerate.

The bracketed case is recoverable at the text layer. The bare-digit case is not: `"if AI is here to stay 3, I'm a software craftsman"` and `"Simultaneous to step 5, I'm also operating"` are the same shape as text, so a rule removing one removes the other. The bare-digit case stays unhandled.

Design: a residual strip over the spoken path, applied to `text` tokens inside `_to_spoken` in `api/app/service/extract.py`, so inline code spans and fenced blocks are protected by the token walk rather than by a guard.

Two rules are settled and not to be reopened:

* Cap at one to three digits. `[1]`, `[12]`, `[123]` and runs like `[1][2]` strip. `[1997]` does not: four digits is a year or a figure number.
* Unicode superscripts (`¹²³`) are left alone. They are not unambiguous: `m⁻¹`, `x²` and `km h⁻¹` are meaningful in scientific writing.

Also left alone: brackets holding a letter (`[sic]`, `[citation needed]`, `[Knuth 1984]`).

Settle first whether this is worth building before an article exhibiting it is in the corpus: every real fixture so far carries markup. If built, a new extraction rule needs a function in `extract.py`, a case in `test_extract.py`, a fixture, and a section or callout in `docs/technical-design/article-extraction.md`.","projectMilestone":{"id":"cb9c8236-7ea7-404c-b9b6-641d87b398d3","name":"Extraction v2"},"priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/asermax/issue/ASE-27/footnote-markers-written-as-plain-text-are-read-aloud","gitBranchName":"asermax/ase-27-footnote-markers-written-as-plain-text-are-read-aloud","createdAt":"2026-09-07T03:39:27.366Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-07T03:39:27.366Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["Bug"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"1fbd98cd-0ebe-444d-b249-dfeb8d65cdda","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-09-07T03:39:27.366Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Agustin Carrasco","createdById":"c8b03f1c-0b66-413e-85b8-f11067346ca8","project":"nagara","projectId":"14d108e2-6712-4129-b37d-e021d5aa2f0b","team":"Asermax","teamId":"c821b24b-23d9-403e-9038-23d9024a2110"}

{"id":"ASE-25","uuid":"f9c4865a-a91d-4ace-9302-86551c0b971b","title":"Unfenced REPL and code inside prose paragraphs is spoken as prose","description":"Design problem: on a code-heavy tutorial, some code reaches the listener spoken as prose. A REPL transcript reads out as `>>> # Floating-point numbers >>> int(10.6) 10 ...`, and a code line reads out with its inline comment, `greeting = "Hello, World!" # This is an inline comment`. The reader sees the code correctly; only the spoken form is wrong.

Found by ear on `realpython.com/python-first-steps/`, during the listen pass that generated the two corpus articles through the real Modal path and scanned every spoken form. A sibling finding on that run (a table cell reading its inline-code backtick) was a clean sanitize gap and is fixed at the table path. This one is separate and deeper.

Root cause: these units are not fenced. trafilatura renders multi-statement REPL and code as one large inline `code` span inside a prose paragraph, mixing an intro sentence with the code, for example `` `10.6` returns `10` instead of `11`. Likewise, `3.25` returns `3`: `>>> # Floating-point numbers >>> int(10.6) 10 ...` ``. `_to_spoken` in `api/app/service/extract.py` unwraps an inline `code` token by emitting its content, which correctly drops the backticks so no marker leaks, but the content is the code itself: `>>>` prompts, `#` comments, statements. Because the block never matched a fence, nothing tagged it `code`, so it was neither described by the describer nor reduced to a placeholder. It is the residue of the same pathological fences the fence-segmentation repair handled: on this article trafilatura's code output is unbalanced and partly flattened.

`sanitize_spoken` already runs on this path and does not help: there is no marker to strip and no clean seam to split on. `10.6 returns 10 instead of 11. Likewise, 3.25 returns 3:` is prose and the REPL after it is code, in one paragraph.

Only one corpus article does this; incidence beyond it is unknown.

Open decisions:

* Detection: how to recognize a prose paragraph carrying flattened REPL or code without misfiring on prose that legitimately quotes a symbol or a short expression. A large inline-code span, or one carrying `>>>`, `$`, or multiple statements, is a candidate signal.
* Handling: whether to split the code into its own unit (so the describer names it) or reduce the inline code to a short placeholder, and how to do either when prose and code share one paragraph.
* Scope: whether to solve this before a second code-heavy article exists to measure incidence, or document it as a known limitation until then. Under Extraction v2, a per-domain recipe for realpython is another way to handle it.

Judge against the cached corpus HTML for that article, not in the abstract. See `docs/technical-design/article-extraction.md` and `docs/technical-design/the-describer.md`.","projectMilestone":{"id":"cb9c8236-7ea7-404c-b9b6-641d87b398d3","name":"Extraction v2"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/asermax/issue/ASE-25/unfenced-repl-and-code-inside-prose-paragraphs-is-spoken-as-prose","gitBranchName":"asermax/ase-25-unfenced-repl-and-code-inside-prose-paragraphs-is-spoken-as","createdAt":"2026-09-07T03:39:15.183Z","updatedAt":"2026-09-07T03:39:15.183Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["Bug"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"1fbd98cd-0ebe-444d-b249-dfeb8d65cdda","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-09-07T03:39:15.183Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Agustin Carrasco","createdById":"c8b03f1c-0b66-413e-85b8-f11067346ca8","project":"nagara","projectId":"14d108e2-6712-4129-b37d-e021d5aa2f0b","team":"Asermax","teamId":"c821b24b-23d9-403e-9038-23d9024a2110"}

content.content:
## 🔭 Overview A recipe is one domain's extraction knowledge: a script that receives an article's HTML as a Cheerio document and returns the article as a title and a list of markdown units, deterministically, so the same page always yields the same units. Agents write recipes. The first article from a domain authors the domain's recipe, and every later article extracts with it. When a recipe fails an article, that article triggers a revision. The model runs at authoring time only. ## 🧾 The script and its declarations A recipe is a script plus the declarations around it. The container selector names the element that contains the article, and everything outside the container is site chrome. The inventory names every element kind the domain's pages carry inside the container and the role each plays: a unit, inline content, a wrapper, or the title. The ignores are the selectors deliberately excluded, each with the judgement that justified it; typical ignores are ads, date stamps and share rows. Every recipe excludes footnote markers and footnote bodies, because the authoring prompts instruct it to. The author prompt and the revision prompt embed one shared contract of plain instructions. The prompts also require GFM markdown. They have the recipe replace every `` element with its alttext as plain text, with no delimiter, before calling `toMarkdown`. The rule covers a block formula and an inline one in a paragraph, list item, table cell or quote alike. The recipe passes the whole element to `toMarkdown`, never a piece of it, and declares a whole list as one unit even when the list holds a code block or an image. They exclude a blockquote's attribution, a `
`, a heading self-link and a heading that repeats the title, and they keep a task list's checkboxes. See [markdown-units](markdown-units.md) for what each of those becomes in a unit's display. The inventory is the union across the domain's pages, and an element kind absent from one page is normal variation across a domain's posts. The script receives the Cheerio document and `toMarkdown`, the fixed HTML-to-markdown converter, from the runtime, and imports nothing. The script reads the document without changing it. Domain knowledge enters as structural preparation of a cloned element. The script builds a `` for a table that lacks one, swaps MathML for the LaTeX in its `alttext`, removes footnote subtrees, and wraps a span-built listing in a `
`. The fixed pass converts the prepared clone.

> [!TIP] Rejected: the agent writes its own conversion
> A trial where the agent hand-converted html to markdown matched the fixed pass on quality and gained nothing by it: conversion stopped being identical across domains, and a recipe could get conversion wrong. The per-domain tricks survived as clone preparation, which is reviewable DOM structure, never a rewritten converter.

## 📦 Units and the fixed pass

Units come back in document order, one element per unit as the recipe declares them, never overlapping: once an element is a unit, everything inside it is that unit's content. The kinds are `paragraph`, `code` and `image`. A paragraph is any flow that renders as markdown: prose, headings, quotes, lists, tables; a list is a single declared unit, even one holding a code block or an image; the nested code block or image stays inside the list's own markdown and never becomes a unit of its own (see [markdown-units](markdown-units.md)). The fixed conversion pass produces a paragraph or code unit's display markdown. An image unit carries `src` and `alt` exactly as the page presents them: the recipe never invents `alt`, and the src is how the recipe resolves the domain's lazy-load conventions. An image the article carries is always emitted, even when its src cannot be resolved. Acquiring, validating, describing or dropping images is downstream's business.

> [!NOTE] Why three kinds and not one per markdown shape
> Downstream distinguishes exactly three things: text rendered as markdown and read as prose, code that gets described instead of read, and images that get acquired and follow the alt precedence. Headings, quotes, lists and tables all derive their display from their markdown, so one paragraph kind covers them; even the read-along table of contents derives from a `#`-prefixed unit's display text, not from a kind.

The same validator runs at authoring, revision and extraction. It checks that every unit's element is inside the container, in document order, none nested inside another; that every element kind in the container is declared or reported as unexpected; that no readable text is left after the units and ignores are removed, with the leftover report naming the element kinds that carry it; and that no declared unit is an `
  • ` on its own. The report line for an orphaned `
  • ` names the unit, the list it belongs to and the rule that a recipe hands a list over whole. It also checks that every unit's markdown is valid: non-empty, no residual HTML outside code, balanced fences. The fence check accepts an opening fence right after a list, quote or task marker, because a list item holding only a code block puts the fence on the marker's own line. Invalid markdown fails a recipe like any other problem.

## 📩 The lifecycle: authoring and revision

First authoring happens when a domain's first article arrives: the base prompt runs against that article's HTML, best-effort within one hundred turns, with one retry of the whole run, and if that fails the item fails with nothing saved for the domain. A domain's homepage enqueued by mistake fails and saves nothing, and the next real article authors fresh.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor L as Listener
    participant P as Item pipeline
    participant A as Agent
    participant V as Recipe runtime
    participant S as Recipe store

    L->>P: Enqueues the article URL
    P->>P: Extract with the
    current version
    P->>P: Validation fails
    P->>A: Iteration prompt +
    current script + report
    Note over P,A: The domain is locked:
    its other articles hold
    alt the page is not an article
        A-->>P: The verdict
        P-->>L: Item fails, the recipe stands
    else a fix
        A->>V: Run the fix
    against this article
        loop within 100 turns,
    then two retries of the run
            V-->>A: Report
            A->>A: Fix additively, re-validate
        end
        V-->>A: Problems none
        A->>S: Insert as the new
    highest version
        S-->>P: New current recipe
        P->>P: The held item re-extracts
    with the new version
        P-->>L: Item proceeds
    else the fix gives up
        A-->>P: No passing version
        P-->>L: Item fails, the old
    version stays current
    end
```

Revision triggers when an article fails validation under the current version. The iteration prompt receives the current script, stored whole, and the validator's report. The standing instruction is additive: keep the recipe's previous assumptions and add what this article needs. The exception is a wholesale markup change, where the agent judges the domain was redesigned and may rewrite the recipe outright. Validation is against the triggering article only. The item that triggered the revision holds while the revision runs, then retries with the new version; the listener sees a slow item and nothing else. A revision that gives up writes no version, so the older one stays current and the next article from the domain triggers revision again. Each attempt is independently bounded.

> [!WARNING] A failed revision leaves the domain exposed
> Every new article from a permanently broken domain triggers one bounded revision attempt before failing, and nothing counts these consecutive attempts: the failures are visible, but the agent spend is unbounded.

> [!NOTE] The not-an-article verdict is what catches the 200-status error page
> A URL serving an HTTP 200 error page extracts cleanly under a generic extractor and reaches `ready` as audio of the error page. An agent looking at the page to author or revise reports the page for what it is. The verdict fails the item, from either prompt. From revision, the verdict also means no version is written and the recipe stands.

## ♠️ What extraction hands the pipeline

| Input | What it is | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| The article's HTML | Firecrawl's rawHtml for the URL | The fetch, which resolves redirects and so decides the domain |
| The recipe | The domain's current version, the script stored whole | The recipe store, by the matched domain |

| Output | What it carries |
|---|---|
| The title | The article's own title; the agent prefers the element that contains it, its judgement when there is none |
| The units | `{ kind, markdown or src+alt }`, document order |
| The verdict | Empty when extraction succeeded; not-an-article or not-accessible fails the item |

The recipe's markdown is the single source of truth: display shows it as-is; the spoken form derives from it generically and never reaches a client, and the API drops a unit whose spoken form has no letter or digit (see [article-extraction](article-extraction.md)). The image handler receives the recipe-declared images, acquires and validates them, and prefers a good alt, then a generated description. When acquisition fails, it drops the image with a degradation. The `og:image` lede has no generic rule; when a page's `og:image` belongs in the article, declaring it is the recipe's judgement.

---

Related: [article-extraction](article-extraction.md) · [markdown-units](markdown-units.md) · [extraction-service](extraction-service.md) · [item-lifecycle](item-lifecycle.md) · [item-contract](item-contract.md) · [persistence-and-storage](persistence-and-storage.md)
## 🌐 Fetching the page

The fetch is a firecrawl scrape. Its raw HTML goes to the extraction service unsegmented. The domain of the final URL, after redirects, picks the recipe. A scrape that cannot reach firecrawl, or returns no HTML, fails the item with a `fetch:` reason. The API writes what each scrape bills to the cost ledger in its own commit (see [persistence-and-storage](persistence-and-storage.md)), so a failed item still records the credit it spent.

The fetch sits behind a `Fetcher` interface with one implementation, so a second fetch strategy is another implementation rather than a branch inside the step.

> [!NOTE] What firecrawl is called with, and why rawHtml
> The scrape asks for `rawHtml` and `markdown` at `proxy="auto"`. The API asks for `rawHtml` rather than firecrawl's cleaned HTML because the cleaning throws away images (9 against 5 on one corpus article), and the recipe declares the article's images from the page's own markup. `markdown` costs no extra credit, so the API requests it as evidence; nothing reads it. `proxy="auto"` bills 1 credit when a basic proxy suffices and 5 on a stealth escalation.

> [!WARNING] firecrawl's output is non-deterministic
> The same URL scraped minutes apart returned a 5x spread in size, and `rawHtml` is post-JavaScript, so it can carry hydrated page chrome a plain fetch never had. The recipe's container and ignores are what keep that chrome out of the units. The spread affects re-recording a test cassette, never a replay, which returns recorded bytes verbatim.

## ⏩ What is not built yet

- **Prose-boilerplate stripping.** Footer donation asides and sponsor mentions arrive as full sentences and reach the audio unless the recipe ignores them. The API does not filter them, because a generic filter risks trimming real content.
- **Quote voice switching.** A listener hears a quote in the one narrator voice, and nobody has yet validated the blockquote audio round-trip end to end.

---

Related: [recipes](recipes.md) · [markdown-units](markdown-units.md) · [extraction-service](extraction-service.md) · [the-describer](the-describer.md) · [item-lifecycle](item-lifecycle.md) · [read-along-timing](read-along-timing.md) · [item-contract](item-contract.md) · [tts-service](tts-service.md) · [persistence-and-storage](persistence-and-storage.md) · [invariants](invariants.md) · [what-gets-read-aloud](../product-design/what-gets-read-aloud.md)

> Every new article from a permanently broken domain triggers one bounded revision attempt before failing, and nothing counts these consecutive attempts: the failures are visible, but the agent spend is unbounded.

> [!NOTE] The not-an-article verdict is what catches the 200-status error page
> A URL serving an HTTP 200 error page extracts cleanly under a generic extractor and reaches `ready` as audio of the error page. An agent looking at the page to author or revise reports the page for what it is. The verdict fails the item, from either prompt. From revision, the verdict also means no version is written and the recipe stands.

## ♠️ What extraction hands the pipeline

| Input | What it is | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| The article's HTML | Firecrawl's rawHtml for the URL | The fetch, which resolves redirects and so decides the domain |
| The recipe | The domain's current version, the script stored whole | The recipe store, by the matched domain |

| Output | What it carries |
|---|---|
| The title | The article's own title; the agent prefers the element that contains it, its judgement when there is none |
| The units | `{ kind, markdown or src+alt }`, document order |
| The verdict | Empty when extraction succeeded; not-an-article or not-accessible fails the item |

The recipe's markdown is the single source of truth: display shows it as-is; the spoken form derives from it generically and never reaches a client, and the API drops a unit whose spoken form has no letter or digit (see [article-extraction](article-extraction.md)). The image handler receives the recipe-declared images, acquires and validates them, and prefers a good alt, then a generated description. When acquisition fails, it drops the image with a degradation. The `og:image` lede has no generic rule; when a page's `og:image` belongs in the article, declaring it is the recipe's judgement.

---

Related: [article-extraction](article-extraction.md) · [markdown-units](markdown-units.md) · [extraction-service](extraction-service.md) · [item-lifecycle](item-lifecycle.md) · [item-contract](item-contract.md) · [persistence-and-storage](persistence-and-storage.md)
## 🌐 Fetching the page

The fetch is a firecrawl scrape. Its raw HTML goes to the extraction service unsegmented. The domain of the final URL, after redirects, picks the recipe. A scrape that cannot reach firecrawl, or returns no HTML, fails the item with a `fetch:` reason. The API writes what each scrape bills to the cost ledger in its own commit (see [persistence-and-storage](persistence-and-storage.md)), so a failed item still records the credit it spent.

The fetch sits behind a `Fetcher` interface with one implementation, so a second fetch strategy is another implementation rather than a branch inside the step.

> [!NOTE] What firecrawl is called with, and why rawHtml
> The scrape asks for `rawHtml` and `markdown` at `proxy="auto"`. The API asks for `rawHtml` rather than firecrawl's cleaned HTML because the cleaning throws away images (9 against 5 on one corpus article), and the recipe declares the article's images from the page's own markup. `markdown` costs no extra credit, so the API requests it as evidence; nothing reads it. `proxy="auto"` bills 1 credit when a basic proxy suffices and 5 on a stealth escalation.

> [!WARNING] firecrawl's output is non-deterministic
> The same URL scraped minutes apart returned a 5x spread in size, and `rawHtml` is post-JavaScript, so it can carry hydrated page chrome a plain fetch never had. The recipe's container and ignores are what keep that chrome out of the units. The spread affects re-recording a test cassette, never a replay, which returns recorded bytes verbatim.

## ⏩ What is not built yet

- **Prose-boilerplate stripping.** Footer donation asides and sponsor mentions arrive as full sentences and reach the audio unless the recipe ignores them. The API does not filter them, because a generic filter risks trimming real content.
- **Quote voice switching.** A listener hears a quote in the one narrator voice, and nobody has yet validated the blockquote audio round-trip end to end.

"""The fetch seam: turn a URL into an article's HTML.

A ``Fetcher`` is the capability interface a fetch implements. The item pipeline fetches
through firecrawl (``FirecrawlFetcher`` here, beside the SDK it drives so a test patches
that library at one place). This module carries the interface, the value types that cross
the seam, and the firecrawl fetcher.

A fetcher is synchronous: the SDK blocks, and the pipeline bridges the call through
``run_in_threadpool`` at the step, matching the codebase's convention of bridging a sync
library at its call site rather than hiding a thread hop inside every fetcher.
"""

from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

from firecrawl import Firecrawl


class ExtractionError(Exception):
    """A fetch or extraction failure whose message already carries its ``fetch:`` or
    ``extraction:`` prefix, so the pipeline's failure write passes it through as the
    item's error."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FetchedPage:
    """One fetched document: the HTML the extraction service segments, and the URL the
    fetch finally landed on.

    ``url`` is the *final* URL — redirects resolved — because the recipe domain is the
    final host, and consolidation across domains comes from exactly those redirects.
    """

    html: str
    url: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FirecrawlUsage:
    """What one firecrawl scrape billed, read off the response. Emitted whenever the scrape
    succeeds, even when it returns no HTML, because the credit is spent on the call."""

    credits: int
    destination: str
    proxy: str | None


class Fetcher(Protocol):
    """Turn a URL into a ``FetchedPage``, or raise ``ExtractionError``. Synchronous by contract."""

    def fetch(self, url: str) -> FetchedPage: ...


class FirecrawlFetcher:
    """A firecrawl scrape as the pipeline's fetch. rawHtml is chosen over firecrawl's cleaned
    HTML because it keeps the images the cleaning drops, and is handed to the extraction
    service unsegmented; markdown rides along at the same credit as evidence, never read.
    ``proxy="auto"`` bills 1 on a basic proxy and 5 on a stealth escalation. Any SDK failure
    is a firecrawl that could not be reached and collapses to one error; the usage callback
    fires the moment the scrape bills, before any empty return."""

    def __init__(self, api_key: str, on_cost: Callable[[FirecrawlUsage], None] | None = None):
        self._api_key = REDACTED
        self._on_cost = on_cost

    @staticmethod
    def _usage_from_document(document: object, url: str) -> FirecrawlUsage:
        # The SDK parses its camelCase response into snake_case metadata (creditsUsed to
        # credits_used). A mock document without metadata reports zero credits and the request
        # URL, which is only ever the no-network unit tests - a real scrape always carries it.
        metadata = getattr(document, "metadata", None)
        return FirecrawlUsage(
            credits=getattr(metadata, "credits_used", None) or 0,
            destination=getattr(metadata, "source_url", None) or url,
            proxy=getattr(metadata, "proxy_used", None),
        )

    def fetch(self, url: str) -> FetchedPage:
        client = Firecrawl(api_key=self._api_key)

entries.description: Create or update a comment on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. If `id` is provided, updates the existing comment; otherwise creates a new one. To start a new thread, pass `body` and exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId` — comments on issues/projects/initiatives become top-level discussion threads; comments on documents/milestones become description comments. A status update holds a single thread, so a comment on an update that already has one is added to it as a reply. To reply to an existing thread, pass `parentId` and `body`; the reply inherits the parent's thread type, so no entity reference is needed. Parent reference fields are ignored when `id` or `parentId` is provided (`statusUpdateType` is rejected instead).

id.description: Comment ID. If provided, updates the existing comment

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Only valid together with `statusUpdateId`; omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

parentId.description: Parent comment ID (for replies, only when creating)

body.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe)

{"id":"ASE-25","uuid":"f9c4865a-a91d-4ace-9302-86551c0b971b","title":"Unfenced REPL and code inside prose paragraphs is spoken as prose","description":"Design problem: on a code-heavy tutorial, some code reaches the listener spoken as prose. A REPL transcript reads out as `>>> # Floating-point numbers >>> int(10.6) 10 ...`, and a code line reads out with its inline comment, `greeting = "Hello, World!" # This is an inline comment`. The reader sees the code correctly; only the spoken form is wrong.

Found by ear on `realpython.com/python-first-steps/`, during the listen pass that generated the two corpus articles through the real Modal path and scanned every spoken form. A sibling finding on that run (a table cell reading its inline-code backtick) was a clean sanitize gap and is fixed at the table path. This one is separate and deeper.

Root cause: these units are not fenced. trafilatura renders multi-statement REPL and code as one large inline `code` span inside a prose paragraph, mixing an intro sentence with the code, for example `` `10.6` returns `10` instead of `11`. Likewise, `3.25` returns `3`: `>>> # Floating-point numbers >>> int(10.6) 10 ...` ``. `_to_spoken` in `api/app/service/extract.py` unwraps an inline `code` token by emitting its content, which correctly drops the backticks so no marker leaks, but the content is the code itself: `>>>` prompts, `#` comments, statements. Because the block never matched a fence, nothing tagged it `code`, so it was neither described by the describer nor reduced to a placeholder. It is the residue of the same pathological fences the fence-segmentation repair handled: on this article trafilatura's code output is unbalanced and partly flattened.

`sanitize_spoken` already runs on this path and does not help: there is no marker to strip and no clean seam to split on. `10.6 returns 10 instead of 11. Likewise, 3.25 returns 3:` is prose and the REPL after it is code, in one paragraph.

Only one corpus article does this; incidence beyond it is unknown.

Open decisions:

* Detection: how to recognize a prose paragraph carrying flattened REPL or code without misfiring on prose that legitimately quotes a symbol or a short expression. A large inline-code span, or one carrying `>>>`, `$`, or multiple statements, is a candidate signal.
* Handling: whether to split the code into its own unit (so the describer names it) or reduce the inline code to a short placeholder, and how to do either when prose and code share one paragraph.
* Scope: whether to solve this before a second code-heavy article exists to measure incidence, or document it as a known limitation until then. Under Extraction v2, a per-domain recipe for realpython is another way to handle it.

Judge against the cached corpus HTML for that article, not in the abstract. See `docs/technical-design/article-extraction.md` and `docs/technical-design/the-describer.md`.","projectMilestone":{"id":"cb9c8236-7ea7-404c-b9b6-641d87b398d3","name":"Extraction v2"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/asermax/issue/ASE-25/unfenced-repl-and-code-inside-prose-paragraphs-is-spoken-as-prose","gitBranchName":"asermax/ase-25-unfenced-repl-and-code-inside-prose-paragraphs-is-spoken-as","createdAt":"2026-09-07T03:39:15.183Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-05T00:23:14.312Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":"2026-10-05T00:23:14.275Z","dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Canceled","statusType":"canceled","labels":["Bug"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Agustin Carrasco","createdById":"c8b03f1c-0b66-413e-85b8-f11067346ca8","project":"nagara","projectId":"14d108e2-6712-4129-b37d-e021d5aa2f0b","team":"Asermax","teamId":"c821b24b-23d9-403e-9038-23d9024a2110"}

{"id":"ASE-26","uuid":"af2bf91d-2c0c-4fd8-b126-18940ad269c2","title":"Strip prose boilerplate: footer, donation and sponsor paragraphs","description":"Spike: strip prose-boilerplate paragraphs that trafilatura leaves in as full sentences, without over-trimming real content.

Footer donation asides and sponsor mentions arrive as complete sentences, so trafilatura's cruft filter does not catch them. Seen on the magazine and newsletter fixtures in the corpus that de-risked the backend pipeline.

The existing cleanup, described in `docs/technical-design/article-extraction.md` and implemented in `api/app/service/extract.py`, only strips safe edge cruft: an echoed title, nav labels, footnote glyphs, punctuation-only units. This is a harder problem, heuristic or per-site, and the risk to manage is trimming real content along with the boilerplate. Under Extraction v2 the per-site half of it is what a recipe is for.

Not yet broken down into something a single probe could settle. It is the accepted residual from promoting the backend pipeline to main: known, not fixed. Any new extraction rule that comes out of this needs a function in `extract.py`, a case in `test_extract.py`, a fixture exhibiting the boilerplate, and a section or callout in the extraction note.","projectMilestone":{"id":"cb9c8236-7ea7-404c-b9b6-641d87b398d3","name":"Extraction v2"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/asermax/issue/ASE-26/strip-prose-boilerplate-footer-donation-and-sponsor-paragraphs","gitBranchName":"asermax/ase-26-strip-prose-boilerplate-footer-donation-and-sponsor","createdAt":"2026-09-07T03:39:21.064Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-05T00:23:16.131Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":"2026-10-05T00:23:16.107Z","dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Canceled","statusType":"canceled","labels":["Spike"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Agustin Carrasco","createdById":"c8b03f1c-0b66-413e-85b8-f11067346ca8","project":"nagara","projectId":"14d108e2-6712-4129-b37d-e021d5aa2f0b","team":"Asermax","teamId":"c821b24b-23d9-403e-9038-23d9024a2110"}

{"id":"ASE-27","uuid":"21e4b4fc-5c22-47f2-a0fb-790d8a561939","title":"Footnote markers written as plain text are read aloud","description":"A footnote marker written as plain text carries no markup to prune, survives to synthesis, and is read aloud.

Footnote reference markers are excluded structurally today: the authoring prompts have every recipe ignore footnote markers and bodies by their markup. A marker with no markup around it is outside that reach: a `[1]` typed into the prose as ordinary text, or a bare digit left behind by a shape the recipe does not recognize.

The bracketed case is recoverable at the text layer. The bare-digit case is not: `"if AI is here to stay 3, I'm a software craftsman"` and `"Simultaneous to step 5, I'm also operating"` are the same shape as text, so a rule removing one removes the other. The bare-digit case stays unhandled.

Design: a residual strip over the spoken path, applied to `text` tokens inside `to_spoken` in `api/app/service/extract.py`, so inline code spans and fenced blocks are protected by the token walk rather than by a guard.

Two rules are settled and not to be reopened:

* Cap at one to three digits. `[1]`, `[12]`, `[123]` and runs like `[1][2]` strip. `[1997]` does not: four digits is a year or a figure number.
* Unicode superscripts (`¹²³`) are left alone. They are not unambiguous: `m⁻¹`, `x²` and `km h⁻¹` are meaningful in scientific writing.

Also left alone: brackets holding a letter (`[sic]`, `[citation needed]`, `[Knuth 1984]`).

Settle first whether this is worth building before an article exhibiting it is in the corpus: every real fixture so far carries markup. If built, a new extraction rule needs a function in `extract.py`, a case in `test_extract.py`, a fixture, and a section or callout in `docs/technical-design/article-extraction.md`.","projectMilestone":{"id":"36312d78-c917-4606-b021-8558f2d060ef","name":"Extraction issues"},"priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/asermax/issue/ASE-27/footnote-markers-written-as-plain-text-are-read-aloud","gitBranchName":"asermax/ase-27-footnote-markers-written-as-plain-text-are-read-aloud","createdAt":"2026-09-07T03:39:27.366Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-05T00:23:18.640Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["Bug"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Agustin Carrasco","createdById":"c8b03f1c-0b66-413e-85b8-f11067346ca8","project":"nagara","projectId":"14d108e2-6712-4129-b37d-e021d5aa2f0b","team":"Asermax","teamId":"c821b24b-23d9-403e-9038-23d9024a2110"}
